Good morning, church. Today we are going to talk about grace. Not the kind of grace you say before a meal, but the grace of God that changes everything. The grace of God is not something we earn. The grace of God is something we receive. And when we receive the grace of God, it changes how we see ourselves, how we see other people, and how we see the world.

Let me start with a story. When I was twelve years old, my father took me fishing on a small lake outside of town. We got up before the sun came up, loaded the truck, and drove for about an hour. I remember being so excited that I could not sit still. My father kept telling me to be patient. Be patient, he said, the fish are not going anywhere. Be patient, the day is long. But I was not patient. I threw my line in the water, and after about five minutes I pulled it back out. I threw my line in the water again, and after five more minutes I pulled it back out again.

By the middle of the morning I had caught nothing, and my father had caught four fish. I was angry. I told him it was not fair. And he looked at me and said something I have never forgotten. He said, son, you cannot catch what you will not wait for.

You cannot catch what you will not wait for. I think about that sentence all the time. Because so many of us want the grace of God, but we want it on our schedule. We want the peace of God, but we want it right now. We want the love of God, but we do not want to slow down long enough to receive it.

The apostle Paul wrote about this in his letter to the church in Rome. He wrote that we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. He wrote that through him we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we now stand. Listen to that again. This grace in which we now stand. Grace is not a place you visit. Grace is a place you stand. Grace is where you live.

So here is what I want you to do this week. First, I want you to slow down. Take ten minutes every morning, before you pick up your phone, before you check your messages, before you do anything else, and just be still. Second, I want you to say thank you. Thank God for the grace you have already received. Thank God for the people in your life. Thank God for this church. And third, I want you to give grace to someone else. Someone in your life needs the same grace that God has given you. Maybe it is someone at work. Maybe it is someone in your family. Maybe it is someone sitting in this room.

When we receive the grace of God, we cannot keep it to ourselves. The grace of God is not something we earn, and it is not something we keep. The grace of God is something we receive, and something we give away. That is the good news. That is why we are here. And that is what changes everything.

Let us pray. Father, thank you for your grace. Thank you that we do not have to earn it. Teach us to slow down. Teach us to be patient. Teach us to receive what you have already given, and teach us to give it away. In the name of Jesus we pray, amen.
